episodes.182666: Even as high pressure began to build into the region, plenty of deep moisture remained entrenched across western Colorado. This led to another round of scattered showers and thunderstorms. Daytime heating and marginal instability fueled some stronger storms, particularly over the higher terrain. One such storm was nearly stationary over the east side of the Grizzly Creek Fire burn scar for an extended period of time, which resulted in some debris flows over I-70. Additionally, heavy rain from storms resulted in debris flows in portions of Ouray County.
episodes.182672: Several days of excessive heat for Middle Tennessee was finally about to come to an end as a cold front approached from the northwest. Thunderstorms developed ahead of this front that moved into western portions of Middle Tennessee during the late afternoon. These thunderstorms produced damaging winds and heavy rain as they moved towards the south. Several reports of wind damage in the form of downed trees and powerlines were received. More significant damage was reported in Spring Hill where a Shell Gas Station's roof collapsed and in Lawrenceburg where a possible microburst caused roofing damage to a motel. Meanwhile, the heavy rain caused minor street flooding in portions of Lawrenceburg and in Williamson County.
episodes.182700: Isolated strong thunderstorms developed during the midday into the early afternoon hours in northeast Alabama producing gusty winds. Later in the afternoon and early evening, a complex of thunderstorms dropped south from middle Tennessee into north Alabama. A strong gust front surged south of the thunderstorms producing wind damage at a few locations in Colbert County in northwest Alabama.
episodes.182808: Two rounds of strong to severe thunderstorms moved through portions of central Indiana initially during the evening hours with a second round during the early overnight. The initial round brought isolated wind damage to areas around Knox county.  Later into the overnight a second round of storms drifted southeast across the Indianapolis area causing additional damage.  At times these thunderstorms moved very slow which caused pockets of flooding with rain amounts in excess of 4 inches in spots.
episodes.183016: A complex of severe thunderstorms moved southeast across southwest Indiana, producing locally damaging winds and pockets of flash flooding. The complex of storms initiated along a stationary front draped from west to east across central Illinois and central Indiana. The storms moved into a very moist and unstable air mass across the lower Ohio Valley, with mixed-layer cape values from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Thunderstorms reformed along and ahead of the front, resulting in training of southeast-moving storms across parts of southwest Indiana.
episodes.183021: A complex of severe thunderstorms moved southeast from southwest Indiana, producing isolated wind damage and street flooding in Henderson County. The complex of storms initiated along a stationary front draped from west to east across central Illinois and central Indiana. The storms moved into a very moist and unstable air mass across the lower Ohio Valley, with mixed-layer cape values from 1500 to 2500 J/kg. Thunderstorms reformed along and ahead of the front, resulting in training of southeast-moving storms across parts of northwest Kentucky.
episodes.183023: A broken line of thunderstorms moved southeast across parts of southeast Missouri. A few of these storms produced strong winds, including isolated wind damage at Poplar Bluff. During the peak heating hours in the mid to late afternoon, thunderstorms gradually increased in coverage along a weak surface boundary over southeast Missouri. Wind shear was weak, but strong instability and high precipitable water values resulted in a wet microburst. Mixed-layer cape ranged from 2500 to 3500 J/kg.
episodes.183053: Scattered instances of strong to marginally severe thunderstorms occurred along the Nebraska-Kansas state line during the afternoon and evening hours of August 25th. Thunderstorms initiated along a southward moving cold front that stalled near the state line during the mid to late afternoon. A brief, transient supercell produced marginally severe hail in Nuckolls County around 5 PM CDT, but the main area of severe weather transpired in Thayer County from a complex of thunderstorms that developed in northwest Kansas then moved eastward along the state line. This activity was sub-severe from 8-10 PM CDT, but then briefly reintensified around 10:30 PM CDT and produced a swath of severe wind. Wind gusts in the 60-65 MPH range were reported, along with crop damage and roof damage to a hotel. The severe portion of the thunderstorm complex exited Thayer County shortly after 11 PM CDT.
episodes.183054: Scattered instances of strong to marginally severe thunderstorms occurred over portions of north central Kansas during the afternoon and evening hours of August 25th. Thunderstorms initiated along a southward moving cold front that stalled near the Nebraska-Kansas state line during the mid to late afternoon. Some strong, but non-severe, wind gusts were reported with the initial scattered development between 5-6 PM in Phillips and Rooks Counties, but the main area of severe weather transpired between 6-8 PM CDT from a complex of thunderstorms that developed in northwest Kansas then organized as it moved eastward along the state line. Severe wind gusts of 60-65 MPH were reported in several parts of Phillips County, while a lone marginally severe hail report occurred in Rooks County. The complex grew in size but decreased in intensity as it moved eastward across the remainder of north central Kansas between 8-11 PM CDT, though a few strong wind gusts continued during this time. Heavy rainfall was also a concern with the thunderstorm complex, and several flood products were issued in the area. However, no impacts beyond typical street or minor low-lying terrain flooding were ultimately reported.
episodes.183372: Thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front and tracked through the area during the late afternoon and early evening hours.  The strongest storms produced hail up to half dollar size.
episodes.183389: A trough of low pressure across the Midlands was the focus for widely scattered strong to severe thunderstorms. The storms produced strong damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183625: A weak surface boundary was draped across the region on August 26. Thunderstorms developed and sagged south along the boundary during the early afternoon, and two brief landspout tornadoes were observed in Fulton County. Neither landspout produced any damage, and thus both were rated EF-Unknown.
episodes.183937: Monsoon moisture brought several pushes of moisture to the region which brought heavy rainfall to most areas, with the daily record in Boise set.
episodes.184119: Outer rainbands from the distant Tropical Cyclone Franklin over the western Atlantic brought unsettled weather conditions across Puerto Rico on August 26th. Between 2 and 4 inches of rain were observed along the southern and eastern half of Puerto Rico. This rainfall resulted in flash flooding, river flooding, and mudslides.
episodes.184143: A cold front moved across northern Arkansas on August 26th and combined with plenty of daytime heating provided sporadic severe thunderstorms across northern and central Arkansas which led to damaging wind gusts.
episodes.184163: An MCS developed along the western portion of the Nebraska and Kansas border. The MCS arrived very late in the evening leading to a few reports of tree damage. The highest measured wind gust was 69 mph near Steinauer in Pawnee County.
episodes.184432: Scattered diurnal convection developed across southern Oklahoma on the evening of the 26th. While wind shear was weak, plentiful instability lead to downburst wind events with the strongest storms. A report of large hail was also received with a briefly organized storm in Murray County, Oklahoma.
episodes.184433: Scattered diurnal convection developed across western-north Texas on the evening of the 26th. While wind shear was weak, plentiful instability lead to downburst wind events with the strongest storm just north of Wichita Falls, Texas.
episodes.184550: The remnants of Tropical Storm Harold lingered across southwest New Mexico with a weak surface low near the Continental Divide.  Isolated thunderstorms develop near the Arizona border and moved north across the Lordsburg Playa producing a wind gust to 68 mph.
episodes.184614: An area of low pressure tracking along a stationary frontal boundary draped along the I-72 corridor triggered clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms from late afternoon of August 25th into the pre-dawn hours of August 26th.  Some of the cells produced wind gusts of 60 to 70 mph, which caused scattered wind damage.
episodes.184631: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.184674: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon. One storm produced a severe wind gust in Greenlee County.
episodes.184675: Across the Lower Ohio Valley, it was a warm summer day with temperatures in the 80s. There wasn't much shear in the atmosphere, but enough moisture and strong instability caused a line of convection to develop and intensify as an outflow boundary from earlier convection dropped south through southern Indiana and north central Kentucky. Severe winds from the storms caused widespread tree and power line damage farther east, east of Interstate 65. A separate thunderstorm caused widespread mature tree damage on a golf course in Crawford County.
episodes.184677: Across the Lower Ohio Valley, it was a warm summer day with temperatures in the 80s. There wasn't much shear in the atmosphere, but enough moisture and strong instability caused a line of convection to develop and intensify as an outflow boundary from earlier convection dropped south through southern Indiana and north central Kentucky. Severe winds from the storms caused widespread tree and power line damage, and two unlucky brothers were injured when they were struck by lightning in Lexington at a golf course.
episodes.184695: A typical summer pattern prevailed with scattered thunderstorms producing occasional gusty winds across the coastal waters.
episodes.184760: An isolated thunderstorm uprooted a tree.
episodes.184806: A 79 mph wind gust at Medicine Lodge.
episodes.184808: One inch hail measured west of Churchill in Cassia County.
episodes.184953: Isolated thunderstorms developed in Central Alabama during the peak heating hours on August 25th and 26th, with damage in Shelby and Autauga counties.
episodes.184955: Abundant moisture along a slow moving cold front led to the development of scattered thunderstorms the afternoon and evenings of Saturday August 26 and Sunday August 27 as an upper level disturbance moved across the Southern Plains. Minor wind damage occurred in several of these storms, primarily across Central Texas.
episodes.184983: A cold front moved south through Virginia, West Virginia, and Kentucky during the afternoon hours, approaching Tennessee and North Carolina. Storms formed a bowing line in advance of this front. Portions of this line produced damaging winds which downed some trees.
episodes.184985: A cold front moved south through Virginia, West Virginia, and Kentucky during the afternoon hours, approaching Tennessee and North Carolina. Storms formed a bowing line in advance of this front. Portions of this line produced damaging winds which downed some trees.
episodes.184992: Scattered showers and storms developed within a moisture rich atmosphere. Three homes in Wilkes County were struck by lightning from these storms.
episodes.185009: A cluster of thunderstorms moved east across Northwest Kansas.  Hail up to golf ball size and wind gusts up to 70 MPH were reported with these storms.  In Norton the torrential rainfall from the storm activity caused water to flow into a residence's basement and a business in downtown.
episodes.185014: Outflow ahead of approaching thunderstorms resulted in a wind gust to 61 mph at the Russell Municipal Airport.
episodes.185066: A woman was killed hiking the Fairyland Loop Trail because of flash flooding.
episodes.185131: Some lingering storms created isolated severe weather across southern Colorado.
episodes.185157: A lone strong thunderstorm cluster developed over Menifee County ahead of a cold front during the late afternoon of the 26th. As the storm moved southeast, it briefly became severe and produced wind damage in at least two locations in Breathitt County. The cluster later dissipated as it moved deeper into Southeast Kentucky during the evening.
episodes.185415: Another typical summertime convective regime was in place for the 26th. With the persistent ridging over the area, the convection had more dry air to work with, so the stronger storms were able to produce damaging winds across parts of southeast Louisiana  before dissipating shortly after sunset.
episodes.185497: On the late afternoon of August 25th, a storm brought damaging wind gusts to Lee's Summit. Several hours later in the early morning hours of August 26th, a storm brought a 63 mph wind gust to St. Joseph Airport.
episodes.186769: A line of storms moved across portions of Lewis County, dropping up to 6 inches of rain in a short amount of time causing flash flooding.
episodes.192673: Heavy rain brought flash flooding to several places in southern Utah.
episodes.192676: Heavy rain resulted in a debris flow in northeast Utah.
